title: Sale prices and real savings
description: A 50% discount is only a saving if you needed the thing at the full price.

body.heading: The anchor trick
paragraphs: Sales work by anchoring: a crossed-out high price makes the sale price feel like a bargain, even if the item rarely sold at the high price. The only honest comparison is with what the item is worth to you and what it costs elsewhere.
Before a sale purchase, check the price history in your head: Have you seen it cheaper? Would you buy it at this price if there were no sale sign?

body.heading: Buy the need, not the discount
paragraphs: A saving on something you did not need is spending wearing a costume. Keep a list of things you genuinely plan to buy, and let sales serve the list — not the other way round.
Stocking up can be smart for things you use constantly, like basic toiletries, if storage and expiry dates allow. For trends and gadgets, the sale will usually come again.

body.heading: Set a sale budget
paragraphs: If you enjoy sales, give them a small budget in advance. You keep the fun of the hunt, and the total stays your decision rather than the shop's.

takeaway: Judge a sale by the item's worth to you, not by the size of the discount.
